title: Collaborative vs Adversarial Debate Under a Weak Judge

original_idea.body:
# Collaborative vs Adversarial Debate Under a Weak Judge

**Problem:** Whether collaboration helps or hurts a weak judge -- by removing adversarial cross-examination -- is unresolved.

**Direction:** Run identical error-detection/QA tasks under adversarial vs collaborative debate with the same small open models and judge. Compare judge accuracy and accuracy on items where agents are jointly wrong (collusion risk).

**Why it matters:** Collaboration could trade a visible failure for a dangerous hidden one.

**Relevant context:** arXiv:2510.20963; Kenton et al. (2024).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: collusion risk in collaborative debate is a subtle hidden oversight regression worth quantifying.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Run two debate modes through the same judge; collaborative multi-agent setup is guided.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused adversarial-vs-collaborative comparison with a collusion metric.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Subtle oversight-regression detection labs deprioritize; external, inference-only.

novelty.reasoning: Collaborative debate just proposed; the weak-judge collusion comparison may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Collaborative debate exists; weak-judge collusion angle plausibly open.
